evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: No other story duplicates the exact requirement of creating a new game with name/description.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL
evaluations.rationale: Inviting via URL is a distinct requirement; no other story requires the same invite mechanism as its primary goal.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: This story specifies starting a round via a single multi-line input, which is not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Moderator view of current-session items is unique; similar estimator story exists but actor differs meaningfully.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item (including re-estimate) is a distinct functional action and not wholly duplicated by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items generally is distinct from starting a round or editing items; no other story duplicates this exact add action.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing list items is a distinct requirement (improving item text); not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item is distinct from deleting games or accounts; unique requirement.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately ... even though not all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: This specific moderator-controlled early reveal behavior is not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting the average as the agreed estimate is a unique business rule; not duplicated.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-fill-on-consensus behavior is a specific feature distinct from showing or accepting estimates.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Manual entry of agreed estimate is distinct from automatic acceptance or averaging features.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Substantially contained by PP-005 which explicitly allows selecting an item to be "re-estimated"; no meaningful difference in actor or goal.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing from a spreadsheet as a specific mechanism is distinct from copy/paste; not a duplicate.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste is a different method/UX than import; the mechanism difference is meaningful and not a duplicate.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games (finding a specific past game) is distinct from viewing a transcript or scrolling within a session.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a game's transcript (stories and estimates) is distinct from browsing or in-session scrolling; unique requirement.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Export as HTML is a distinct output format; not duplicated by other stories that export different formats.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Export as CSV differs in format and use-case from HTML export; not a duplicate.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game is different from deleting items or accounts; unique requirement.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Account creation with specified fields is unique; no duplicate story requires the exact same inputs.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Login requirement is distinct from account creation, deletion, or password reminders.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Updating account details is unique from creating/deleting accounts or logging in.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion is a unique action; not duplicated by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display requirement is specific and not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder by email is a distinct recovery feature; no duplicate.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Selecting estimation scale (Fibonacci vs powers of two) is a unique configuration requirement.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: The explicit team size limit is a business rule not duplicated by the general invite story.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via URL and entering a name is distinct from the moderator's invite action.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Participant's need to view the current item is a unique requirement; no duplicate found.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Estimator-focused view of the session item list is distinct from the moderator's equivalent (PP-004) due to actor/context.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Real-time indicator of who has already given an estimate differs in goal from stories that show full estimates or mapping of who gave what.

evaluations.evidence: shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Simultaneous reveal after all estimates is a distinct timing rule (ensures independence) not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: This explicit condition for when estimation can be changed is a concrete behavior; another story repeats it (PP-041) and is therefore the duplicate.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Request to view an estimator's prior estimates for the same story is a specific feature distinct from scrolling prior rounds.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Showing the mapping of estimates to people during the round supports discussion and is distinct from merely knowing who has played a card.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Introducing a shared countdown timer is a unique interactive feature; not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Automatic reset behavior tied to all estimates being played is distinct from simply starting a timer.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: In-session scrolling through prior rounds is different from viewing a saved transcript or browsing previous games.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Ensuring consistent card order is a specific UI requirement not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Substantially the same as PP-034 which specifies the same condition (change until last person selects/all shown); no meaningful difference in actor/context/goal.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Adding a thumbnail photo near played cards is a distinct personalization feature; not duplicated.

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Developer requirement for standards compliance is unique and not duplicated by other developer stories.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Creating a definitions list is a distinct documentation task; not duplicated.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Database indexing as a developer performance task is unique; others reference performance but not this exact action.

evaluations.evidence: application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Browser compatibility requirement for specific old browsers is unique and not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a distinct developer concern and not duplicated by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance from a user's perspective is distinct from developer tasks like indexing; not a duplicate requirement.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a specific internationalization requirement not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design requirement is unique and not duplicated by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Custom error pages is a specific UX requirement and not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Anonymized storage for research is a unique privacy requirement not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Metrics/dashboard requirement is distinct and not duplicated by other stories.
